basics.name: Xiaopan Zhang
basics.label: Third-year Ph.D. Student in Machine Learning
basics.summary: Third-year Ph.D. student in Machine Learning at the Georgia Institute of Technology, advised by Prof. Jiachen Li. Research interests include embodied AI agents, multi-robot systems, reinforcement learning in robotics, trustworthy autonomy, and robot navigation.

work.name: Georgia Institute of Technology
work.summary: Research on embodied AI agents and multi-robot systems, advised by Prof. Jiachen Li.
highlights: Developing an intervention-guided framework for mobile manipulation that traces failures across navigation, perception, and contact, coordinates physical recovery, and selectively adapts robot skills, residual controllers, and VLA policies to improve long-term autonomy and task performance.

Developed object-goal navigation methods using foundation models as reward generators for reinforcement learning, enabling semantic, task-aware, goal-conditioned decisions without continuous high-latency foundation-model queries.

work.name: Honda Research Institute USA, Inc. (HRI-US)
highlights: Developed SituLaMP, an LLM/VLM-based framework for long-horizon multi-robot planning, execution-time failure detection, dynamic replanning, and task reallocation while preserving unaffected plan structure.

Implemented PDDL planning, multi-robot simulation, and recovery logic for action, perception, and environmental failures, enabling robust online execution and localized recovery across heterogeneous robot teams.

Designed benchmark experiments across multi-robot and embodied-agent tasks to evaluate task completion, robustness, recovery efficiency, generalization, and recovery cost across diverse execution failures.

work.name: AlphaZ, Inc.
highlights: Developed StratMamba, a dual-stream Mamba-based PPO architecture that separates reactive obstacle processing from strategic goal-directed navigation for efficient LiDAR-based obstacle avoidance in cluttered environments.

Built scalable training and evaluation pipelines in IsaacLab and Gazebo for obstacle-rich navigation with quadruped and wheeled robots, and deployed the learned policy on a real Unitree GO1 robot using ROS2, RSLidar-16, VICON localization, and real-time velocity control.
Benchmarked against LSTM, Transformer, and vanilla Mamba baselines, improving timeout rate, path efficiency, navigation speed, and sim-to-real robustness. The work resulted in an IROS 2026 paper.

work.name: Trustworthy Autonomous Systems Laboratory, University of California, Riverside
work.summary: Research on trustworthy multi-agent robotic systems (coordination, task allocation, object-goal navigation), advised by Prof. Jiachen Li.
highlights: Conducted research on trustworthy embodied and multi-agent robotic systems spanning coordination, task allocation, object-goal navigation, uncertainty calibration, and long-horizon planning, resulting in multiple peer-reviewed publications.

Developed object-goal navigation methods using foundation models as reward generators for reinforcement learning, enabling semantic, task-aware, goal-conditioned decisions without continuous high-latency foundation-model queries.

Designed heterogeneous multi-agent planning and communication frameworks for long-horizon, multi-objective tasks in partially observable environments, with capability-aware task allocation and calibrated inter-agent information exchange.

Proposed a two-stage fine-tuned reasoning model (supervised fine-tuning + reinforcement learning) that directly generates executable PDDL plans, enabling adaptive multi-robot task allocation without heuristic search.

Integrated learning-based policies with classical planning and safety constraints to improve robustness, generalization, reliability, and deployment readiness across real-world robotic systems and environments.

work.name: Dynamic Robotics and Control Laboratory, University of Southern California
work.summary: Task allocation, path planning, and coordination for teams of quadruped robots, validated in simulation and in strawberry and raspberry fields.
highlights: Contributed to a large-scale multi-robot project that controls multiple quadruped (four-legged) robots for enhanced exploration and task execution.
Developed task allocation, path planning, and coordination strategies for coordinated exploration with quadruped robot teams.
Conducted extensive testing, validation, and data collection of multi-robot collaboration in simulation and in real-world agricultural environments, including strawberry and raspberry fields.

projects.name: CoReNav: Conformal Calibrated Foundation Model Rewards for Object Navigation
highlights: Proposed a compute-efficient object-goal navigation framework that combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning fine-tuning driven by foundation-model-based rewards, enabling semantically guided exploration without continuous high-latency model querying.

Applied conformal prediction to calibrate foundation-model outputs in the navigation loop, including VLM-based room classification and LLM-generated object relevance priors, producing trust-aware rewards that mitigate hallucinations and stabilize RL fine-tuning.
Evaluated on the HM3D Semantics dataset, showing improvements over baselines in success rate, path optimality, and time efficiency in photo-realistic environments.

projects.name: CommCP: Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination via LLM-Based Communication with Conformal Prediction (ICRA 2026)
highlights: Formulated the information-gathering process for natural-language assignments as a multi-agent multi-task embodied question answering (MM-EQA) problem, where robots collaborate in a shared environment and communicate to exchange information and answers.

Proposed CommCP, an LLM-based decentralized communication framework for MM-EQA that uses conformal prediction to calibrate generated messages, reducing distractions to other agents while improving communication reliability and efficiency.
Created an MM-EQA benchmark with photo-realistic scenarios from the HM3D dataset and released it to facilitate future research.

projects.name: LaMMA-P: Generalizable Multi-Agent Long-Horizon Task Allocation and Planning with LM-Driven PDDL Planner (ICRA 2025)
highlights: Introduced LaMMA-P, a framework that integrates LLM reasoning with PDDL planning heuristics to solve long-horizon task planning for heterogeneous robot teams with a flexible number of agents.

Developed a modular system design that connects LLMs, PDDL planners, and simulation environments to support flexible task decomposition and efficient sub-task allocation based on robot skills and capabilities.
Created MAT-THOR, a benchmark of multi-agent long-horizon tasks based on AI2-THOR with standardized tasks and metrics, achieving state-of-the-art success rate and efficiency.
